overview.description: Nine Card Brag (often called 'Crash') is the final evolution of the multi-card Brag family. Players are dealt nine cards and must divide them into three independent three-card hands. These hands are compared against opponents' corresponding hands in three separate 'showdowns' (front, middle, and back). It combines the traditional British Brag hand rankings with the partition complexity of Chinese Poker, creating a high-stakes duel of distribution and nerve.

history.origins: Originating in the card rooms of Northern England and Scotland, 9-Card Brag emerged as a more complex alternative to the simpler vying variants. It likely took inspiration from the global 'partition' genre while strictly adhering to the centuries-old Brag combination hierarchy.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Multi-hand Brag variants evolve in British social clubs.
1970s: The name 'Crash' becomes synonymous with the 13-card and 9-card partition versions.
Present: A competitive staple in the UK Brag community, often played for high stakes.
history.evolution: The game shifted from a vying focus (betting) toward a scoring focus (winning individual hand comparisons), although many gambling variants still include an initial betting round.
history.cultural: Regarded as the 'Professional' version of Brag, where the luck of the draw is minimized by the skill of the partition.

setup.equipment: Standard pack, score pad or chips.
setup.dealing: Deal nine cards face-down to each player. Players then divide their hand into three separate 3-card Brag combinations.

rules.objective: Win the majority of the three hand comparisons against your opponents.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Partition**: Players divide 9 cards into Hand 1, Hand 2, and Hand 3. 2. **Ordering**: Some variants require hands to be ordered from strongest to weakest. 3. **Comparison**: Hands are revealed one at a time. The winner of each comparison (e.g., Hand 1 vs. Hand 1) scores a point. 4. **Ranks**: Prial (3-3-3 is highest) > Running Flush > Run > Flush > Pair > High Card.
keyRules: All three hands must be valid Brag combinations.
A player who wins all three comparisons is said to have 'Crashed' or 'Swept', often winning a bonus.
Tied comparisons usually result in the point being carried over or shared.

strategy.basic: Don't put all your best cards in one hand. Winning one comparison and losing two will lose you the round. Aim for three balanced 'Pairs' rather than one 'Prial' and two junk hands.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Middle' Trap: Many players put their second-best cards in the middle hand. If you put your best cards in the middle, you can often steal a point from someone who played traditionally.
strategy.advanced: Range Splitting: Evaluate the deck's remaining strength. If you hold many Spades, expect opponents to be weak in sequences and strong in pairs. Adjust your partition to beat pairs with low sequences (Runs).
tips: In 9-Card Brag, a Flush is a 'medium' hand; don't rely on it to win the front hand.
Count the Aces—there are only four. If you have two, the odds of an opponent holding a Prial of Aces is near zero.

list.emptyOverridesReason: This variation links the related 13-card Crash game; engine overrides for that larger partition are not yet modeled.

difficulty.easy: Partitions hands blindly. Does not understand hand-balancing strategy.
difficulty.medium: Uses a greedy solver to make the two strongest hands possible. Understands basic Brag hierarchy.
difficulty.hard: Full combinatorial optimization (9-choose-3-choose-3). Predicts opponent partitions based on known card distributions. Maximizes round-win probability.

considerations: Multi-hand resolution logic must handle ties and bonus sweeps.

additional: Rules of British Partition Games (Historical Society)

ante.reason: 9-Card Brag is typically scored via points per hand rather than using a monetary ante system.

deal.reason: The initial distribution of nine cards to all players is performed automatically by the system dealer.

reveal_market.reason: This is a closed-hand partition game where all cards are held privately; no shared market exists.

buy_market.reason: Players cannot purchase cards from a market; hand strength is fixed after the initial deal.

buy_stock.reason: The entire hand is distributed at the start; no drawing or buying from the stock is permitted during play.

fold.reason: Players must participate in all hand comparisons to determine the final point tally for the round.

check.reason: The game uses a partition and reveal structure rather than a vying structure with checks and bets.

call.reason: There is no pot or bet to match in this variant; competition is based on hand strength comparisons.

bet.reason: Success is measured by points earned in individual comparisons rather than through wagering of assets.

raise.reason: The value of the deal is fixed by game rules and cannot be raised through wagering rounds.

declare.reason: Hand results are established during the showdown comparison rather than through a formal declaration.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands remain private until the system triggers the comparison logic at the end of the partition phase.

award_pot.reason: Winning results in point accumulation on a scorecard rather than distributing a physical pot of chips.

play_card.reason: 9-Card Brag is a partition game where hands are compared rather than played to individual tricks.

draw.reason: Each player receives nine cards at the start and no further drawing occurs during the play of the hand.

discard.reason: Every card in the nine-card deal must be partitioned into the three hands; no cards are discarded.

pass.reason: Players must always provide a complete partition of their hand; passing a turn is not supported.

bid.reason: Bidding is not used in the point-scoring version of 9-Card Brag; game objectives are fixed.

meld.reason: Hand resolution is based strictly on three-card poker hierarchies rather than forming melds.

go_out.reason: The hand terminates only after all three comparisons have been performed by the system dealer.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: All cards are distributed at the start of the hand; no draw pile exists during the partition phase.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: All cards must be partitioned into three hands; no waste or discard pile is utilized in this variant.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Cards contribute only their rank and suit values to combinations; no individual card has a secondary effect.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: Results are immediate upon revealing the partitions; no hidden tokens or chips are used.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: 9-Card Brag is a partition game and does not use a capture-from-tableau fishing mechanic.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: This game is not a shedding game; players maintain their hands throughout the deal.

customActions.description: Distribute nine cards face-down to each player clockwise.
Divide the nine dealt cards into three separate three-card Brag hands.
Bet on the hand without looking at the chosen three cards.
Pay double price to see the cards before betting.
Bet on the hand after paying to see the cards.
Request a showdown to determine the winner between remaining players.
Compare the first three-card hand against opponent's corresponding hand.
Compare the second three-card hand against opponent's corresponding hand.
Compare the third three-card hand against opponent's corresponding hand.
Award points based on the results of the three hand comparisons.

engine.handRankingSystem: None; specialized Brag hierarchy determines the winning hands at showdown.
engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks from ace down to two. No jokers; used for nine-card Brag where prials, runs, and flushes are ranked and ace may be high or low in runs.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). Flushes (nine of the same suit) and running flushes (nine consecutive ranks in the same suit) are ranked hands. Suits do not break ties between equal hand types in Brag.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit; for prials the three is the highest rank, then two, ace, king down to four. For runs, ace may be high or low. Standard Brag order: prial of threes best, then runs, then flushes, then pairs, then high card.

hero.title: NINE CARD BRAG
hero.subtitle: The Triple Threat
hero.tagline: Nine cards. Three hands. One sweep to glory.

synthesis.shortDescription: The strategic peak of the Brag family. Partition nine cards into three independent units and face your opponent across three simultaneous showdowns. Master the math of the split and the bluff of the front hand to become the ultimate Nine Card champion.

prompts.human: You were dealt a Prial of Aces and a Running Flush! But your third hand is junk. Do you split your power cards to ensure you win two comparisons, or go for the 'Crash' bonus by trying to sweep all three?
prompts.ai: Game: Nine Card Brag. Type: Partition. Rules: 9 cards dealt, split into 3 hands of 3. Brag rankings apply. Hands compared sequentially. Win 2/3 to win the round.

scoring.description: Points are awarded for each winning hand comparison. Bonus points for winning all three (the Crash).
scoring.winCondition: Win the majority of hand comparisons in the round.
scoring.splitRules: None; the round must proceed until comparisons are decisive.

nullReasons.targetScore: No fixed target score; play by hand count.
nullReasons.cardValues: Individual cards determine hand rankings rather than having point values.
